A three-hour group sightseeing tour with an English-speaking guide.
Explore Argentina’s capital and discover the history and art behind its centuries-old culture. Buenos Aires is home to many of the country’s best-known sights. Its architecture is often compared to Paris, and the city has a character all its own. Art lovers will find a wide range of museums, galleries, theatres and architectural landmarks. See the old neighbourhood of La Boca and historic San Telmo, with bars and restaurants of all sizes and the antiques market in Plaza Dorrego. The central Plaza de Mayo is the heart of Buenos Aires. Landmarks include the pink presidential palace, Casa Rosada, associated with Evita Perón, and the city’s emblematic 67-metre Obelisk, associated with the proclamation of Argentina’s independence. You’ll also visit elegant Recoleta, with its famous cemetery, the colonial-style El Pilar church and the nearby cultural and commercial centre. The tour also takes in modern Puerto Madero and the parks of Lezama and Tres de Febrero.

In the evening, enjoy a tango show with dinner. Tango is popular around the world, and Argentina is where it began. On stage, the dancers bring its passion, virtuosity and grace to life. The dance took shape in the city’s port districts among poor immigrants, gauchos and others on the margins. Early tango was danced by two men in a bold, uninhibited style. One account traces its name to the Latin tangere, meaning ‘to touch’. Over time, the dance slowed and became more intimate, and orchestras began to play tango. It quickly gained popularity and remains one of the world’s most sensual dances, with room for candour, gallantry and tenderness. The restaurant’s décor sets the scene for the show, and dinner features several traditional dishes and Argentine wines.
The pink Casa Rosada behind a flower bed in Buenos Aires, Argentina
